newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian-led consortium to build Hungary motorway.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian-led consortium to build Hungary motorway.

text.p: A Hungarian-led consortium will construct a 43 km long part of Hungary's M3 motorway, a project to be financed partly by Germany's Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau and the European Investment Bank (EIB).

M Harom Konzorcium, the winner of an international tender with Italian, German, Austrian and Portuguese participants, is led by Hungary's Betonutepito Nemzetkozi Rt, the Transport, Telecommunications and Water Ministry (KHVM) said on Friday.
Members of the consortium are Hungary's Magyar Aszfalt Kft, Hidepito Rt and Austria's Ilbau GmbH, KHVM said in a statement.
Works will start next month and are to be completed by September 1, 1998, secretary of state Kalman Kovacs told a news conference.
Construction costs of the motorway between Gyongyos and Fuzesabony, north-east Hungary will amount to 23.9 billion forints plus VAT, a KHVM statement said.

In addition to budget sources EIB will grant 95 million ECUs and Kreditanstalt will provide 127 million marks. The loans have to be repaid in 20 and 18 years, respectively, after a five-year grace period.
The construction is part of a project to upgrade and build a 100 km long motorway between Budapest and Fuzesabony.
Reconstruction works on the Budapest-Gyongyos part of the M3 motorway began in August by Portugal's Mota & Companhia. -- Emese Bartha, Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327-4040
